ruling: Allow two reserved lab-only error-response egress markers in the proposed design: QA-to-M and M-to-host, each added only to an exact already-selected fresh error Response, with no inbound/forwarded header, added RPC/snapshot/wait, or product deployment.
why: One M-to-host marker cannot bind the QA-returned value across transport. QA's returned non-ok value needs its own closed diagnostic carrier before associating the M error and final returned response. This corrects a load-bearing design gap without changing decisions/status/body or clocks.

QA marker writer is unique to exact first DROP epoch and the Response actually returned for that Request. Require absent marker/canonical version/domain-separated UUID hash/exact actual status, no raw IDs.
M associates D only after validating that response's QA marker/request/status/selector. Then label the error which actually wins, preserving original race/cancel/waitUntil.
M host marker added only after original S03 fetch fulfills with the exact bridge-tagged Response and its finally completed. Host consumes only its exact Response before original discard.

Value provenance under a closed pinned transport, not cross-isolate JS object identity, authentication, or a native-receipt claim. If a fallback can synthesize/reemit marker fields from another invocation, attribution must stay UNKNOWN.
Do not infer public QA site on missing/late/duplicate/stale/wrong marker/status/form/request, unverified map, header collision/immutable guard/helper failure or substituted unmarked result.
